company: Perusahaan Perseroan (Persero) PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (PT Antam (Persero) Tbk)
title: Corporate Securities Trading Policy (Annex to Decision of the Board of Directors Number 38.K/09/DAT/2008)
date_approved: 18 February 2008 (Board of Directors of PT Antam (Persero) Tbk, Decision Number 38.K/09/DAT/2008, stipulated in Jakarta)
date_next_review: No fixed date; the Policy 'will be renewed from time to time' and the Corporate Secretary division must revise it when necessary to adapt to changes in laws and regulations

tiers.name: Company Insiders
tiers.description: Commissioners, directors or employees of the Company; major shareholders; individuals who by their position, profession or business relation with the Company are allowed to gain Insider Information; and any party who ceased to be such within the past 6 months. 'Position' means office in government organisations, institutes or bodies; 'business relation' includes customer, supplier, contractor, client and creditor relationships. Every substantive prohibition in the Policy attaches to this tier without differentiation.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Company Directors, a defined term in the General Provisions and a listed category of Company Insider. No separate rules, approver or reporting deadline is specified for them.

tiers.name: Special Relationship
tiers.description: An individual or body considered as having a special relationship with the Company: an employee of the Company, or a person who has, or submits a proposal in order to have, a business relationship or professional activity with or for the interest of the Company or its subsidiaries.

tiers.name: consultants, brokers, and other people interacting with the company
tiers.description: Consultants, brokers and other people interacting with the Company, its units or subsidiaries, including sales agents and partners in joint ventures, who gain or have access to Material Non-public Information or Fact. The Policy applies to them as it does to Company Insiders.

tiers.name: families, including all their close relatives
tiers.description: Families, including all close relatives, of persons within the scope of the Policy. Those persons are responsible for ensuring their families' compliance with the Policy. The Policy does not name spouses, dependants, trusts or controlled entities specifically.

windows.start_anchor: after the company has disseminated information regarding quarterly, annual or end of year financial statements
windows.end_anchor: the day of trading closing one day before a quarter or a semester ends

windows.start_anchor: 30 March each year (or the closing time of the last trading day before the weekend if 30 March falls on a Sunday)
windows.end_anchor: when the company disseminates the information which previously was non-public information, which the company always does after the market has closed

windows.start_anchor: 29 June each year (or the closing time of the last trading day before the weekend if 29 June falls on a Sunday)
windows.end_anchor: when the company disseminates the information which previously was non-public information

windows.start_anchor: 29 September each year (or the closing time of the last trading day before the weekend if 29 September falls on a Sunday)
windows.end_anchor: when the company disseminates the information which previously was non-public information

windows.start_anchor: 30 December each year (or the closing time of the last trading day before the weekend if 30 December falls on a Sunday)
windows.end_anchor: when the company disseminates the information which previously was non-public information

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company Securities Trading Compliance Supervisory Officer (the Senior Vice President Corporate Secretary, or the Assistant Senior Manager Investor Relations in their absence) decides and announces special trading blackout periods in which no Company Insider at all may trade, and the company also applies a Blackout Period in certain situations where changes result in Material Information or Facts. These are confidential: Company Insiders are not allowed to disclose to any outside party that a certain blackout period has been determined. The Company may also ask Insiders not to trade for a particular reason outside a routine Blackout Period, which is why every trade must be reported in advance.

rules.detail: An outright ban on option or position trading referable to the future price of Company Securities, naming puts and calls. There is no venue limitation, no exception for hedging an existing holding, and no approval or waiver route: the Policy's only procedural gateway is advance reporting of permitted trades, not approval of prohibited ones. The definition of Company Securities is limited to instruments issued by the Company, but clause 5(e) operates on positions 'in relation to' their future price and so reaches derivatives written by a bank.
rules.evidence: Every Company Insider is prohibited to conduct option or position trading in relation to the future (future price) of Company Securities such as put, call, or short sale.

rules.detail: The Policy never uses the words hedging or economic risk and has no clause directed at protecting a shareholding. Hedging is nonetheless caught because the instruments used to do it, puts and calls, are the very positions banned by clause 5(e). No distinction is drawn between unvested plan securities, vested restricted securities and freely held shares.
rules.evidence: prohibited to conduct option or position trading in relation to the future (future price) of Company Securities such as put, call, or short sale.

rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and exchangeables are not named. Such a structure is a 'position' taken in relation to the future price of Company Securities and so falls within clause 5(e); an outright sale of shares to raise cash remains permitted in a trading window on advance report.
rules.evidence: Every Company Insider is prohibited to conduct option or position trading in relation to the future (future price) of Company Securities

rules.detail: Short sale is named in the same clause as puts and calls and is prohibited at all times, in and out of trading windows, with no approval route.
rules.evidence: such as put, call, or short sale.

rules.detail: Securities lending is nowhere mentioned and there is no defined term 'dealing' that could sweep it in. The nearest provision is clause 5(f), which bars an Insider from giving or causing anyone to transfer Company Securities during a period in which they are not allowed to trade, so a stock loan delivery inside a blackout would be caught by that clause.

Contracts for difference are not named, but a CFD is a position taken in relation to the future price of Company Securities and, if short, is also a short sale, so it is prohibited on both limbs of clause 5(e).
rules.evidence: Every Company Insider is prohibited to conduct option or position trading in relation to the future (future price) of Company Securities such as put, call, or short sale.

rules.detail: Margin lending is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy. There is no prohibition, no approval requirement, no gearing or price trigger guidance, and no disclosure obligation, though the Policy's advance reporting requirement would apply to any trade in Company Securities associated with such an arrangement.

Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge over Company Securities is not addressed and is not within any definition. Clause 5(f) does prohibit an Insider from giving or causing anyone to transfer Company Securities during a period in which they may not trade, which would bite on a transfer of legal title to a collateral holder inside a blackout period.

The Policy contains no provision on borrowing against Company Securities, whether by margin loan or bespoke facility, and no reporting obligation attaches to the grant of security. This is a genuine gap rather than a permission: the trading and derivative prohibitions still govern any dealing in the shares themselves.

There is no minimum holding period, no LIFO or buy-sell window rule and no speculative trading prohibition. Timing is controlled solely by the trading window and blackout period structure, which in practice confines trading to the weeks after each quarterly or annual results dissemination.

clearance.approver: Company Securities Trading Compliance Supervisory Officer, being the Senior Vice President Corporate Secretary or, when the Corporate Secretary Officer is not present or unavailable, the Assistant Senior Manager Investor Relations
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Securities Trading Compliance Supervisory Officer
clearance.post_trade_deadline: after a Company Securities trading transaction has been done; no deadline stated
clearance.evidence: every trading of Company Securities by Company Insiders must be reported in advance to the Company Securities Trading Compliance Supervisory Officer. There shall be a notification complete with the reason of why the trading is carried out and a statement that the concerned party is not in the condition if having in possession any Material Non-public Information or Fact.

exceptions.evidence: These procedures do not apply for the purchase of Company Securities which has been set in Employee Stock Purchase Plan or for exercise of option over company’s stock which has been set in Corporate Equity Incentive Plan.

exceptions.approver: Company Securities Trading Compliance Supervisory Officer (to be consulted where an Insider is uncertain about other prohibitions or restrictions)
exceptions.evidence: Prohibitions and restrictions of trading stipulated in this Policy may not be applicable due to the existence of prohibitions and restrictions stipulated by higher law provisions and regulations.

external_documents: Company Information Disclosure Policies, which specify the parties falling within the legal business purpose exception
Indonesia Law Number 8 Year 1995 concerning Capital Market
Decision of the Board of Directors Number 38.K/09/DAT/2008, to which this Policy is an annex
exemption_authority: None. The Policy provides no hardship, court order, exceptional circumstances or discretionary waiver of any prohibition. The Company Securities Trading Compliance Supervisory Officer administers and interprets the Policy, answers questions, decides and announces special blackout periods and revises the Policy, but is given no power to permit a prohibited activity; clause 8(a) merely recognises that higher law may displace the Policy's restrictions.
jurisdiction_overlays: Indonesian Capital Market Law (Law Number 8 Year 1995) and supervision by the Indonesian Capital Market Supervisory Agency (BAPEPAM), with Article 104 penalties of up to 10 years imprisonment and a fine of up to Rp 15,000,000,000

Australian capital market authority regulation, the Company being registered on both the Indonesian and Australian stock exchanges; the Corporate Secretary division must administer compliance with the laws of both exchanges

bespoke_clauses.clause: Every Company Insider is prohibited to conduct option or position trading in relation to the future (future price) of Company Securities such as put, call, or short sale.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both legs of a collar, the purchased put and the written call, are named prohibited positions, so the derivative side of the structure is impossible for any Insider with no approval route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Company Insiders include: commissioners, directors, or employees of the Company; Major shareholders of the Company; Individuals who, due to their position or profession or to their business relation with the Company, are allowed to gain Insider Information; or Any parties which, within the past 6 (six) months, no longer become any Party referred to above. 'Business relation' ... includes customer relation, supplier, contractor, client, and creditor.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank that becomes a creditor of the Company could itself fall within the Insider definition, and a departing executive remains an Insider for six months, so the prohibition follows the client past resignation.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Every Company Insider is prohibited to give or cause anyone to transfer Company Securities during a period where they are not allowed to conduct trading.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Delivery of collateral, physical settlement or a financier's enforcement sale occurring inside a blackout would be an Insider causing a transfer when not permitted to trade, and there is no lender enforcement carve-out.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Company Insiders are not allowed to disclose to any outside party that a certain blackout period has been determined.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A client cannot tell a bank why an execution, roll or unwind is being delayed, so a facility must tolerate unexplained inability to act.

bespoke_clauses.topic: quarterly closed periods with open-ended end
bespoke_clauses.clause: Blackout period commences on 30 March, 29 June, 29 September, and 30 December every year and ends when the company disseminates information which previously is non-public information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Four blackouts a year, each of indeterminate length because it ends only on results dissemination, leaves narrow and unpredictable windows for any transaction in the shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no reference to margin lending, secured financing, pledges, charges or securities lending.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg secured on the shares is neither prohibited nor regulated, so it is governed only by Indonesian law and the Company's other rules, and a bank would need separate confirmation from the Corporate Secretary rather than reliance on this Policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: every trading of Company Securities by Company Insiders must be reported in advance to the Company Securities Trading Compliance Supervisory Officer. ... Company Insiders are required to report/confirm to the Company Securities Trading Compliance Supervisory Officer after a Company Securities trading transaction has been done.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The regime is notification rather than approval, with no validity period or response time, so any permitted share transaction supporting a financing must be pre-notified with reasons and confirmed afterwards.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The parties included in the scope of this Policy are also responsible for ensuring the compliance of their families, including all their close relatives with this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The prohibitions cannot be avoided by placing the position with a family member, although the Policy does not extend expressly to trusts or controlled companies.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy is a 2008 board decision translated from Indonesian, with no review date, no derivatives or financing framework and no cross-reference to ASX Listing Rule 12.12 content requirements.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Its silences should be treated as gaps to be checked with the Corporate Secretary rather than as permissions, and a bank should confirm no later Indonesian or ASX-facing policy supersedes it.

summary: A funded collar is not possible for a PT Antam Company Insider, because the derivative legs are expressly banned. Clause 5(e) prohibits every Company Insider from conducting option or position trading in relation to the future price of Company Securities, naming put, call and short sale, with no venue limitation, no distinction between vested and unvested holdings and no approval, hardship or exceptional circumstances waiver anywhere in the Policy. The funding leg is a different matter: margin lending, secured financing, pledges and securities lending are simply not addressed, so a loan secured on the shares is unregulated by this Policy, though clause 5(f) prohibits an Insider from giving or causing anyone to transfer Company Securities during a period in which they may not trade, which would catch collateral delivery or an enforcement sale inside a blackout. Any permitted transaction in the shares themselves must fall in a trading window, outside the blackouts commencing 30 March, 29 June, 29 September and 30 December and outside any confidential special blackout, and must be reported in advance to the Company Securities Trading Compliance Supervisory Officer with reasons and confirmed afterwards. Given the Policy's age, its translation from Indonesian and its silence on financing, a bank should verify the position with the Corporate Secretary rather than infer permission from the gaps.
